decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with left arm toward the mallet handle; raise and tilt wrist gradually. Right arm stays parked.
Approach above the handle while rotating the open gripper to align along the mallet shaft; maintain elbow-up continuity.
Finish top-down alignment over the left end of the handle, staying above it before closing.
Center the shaft in the wrist view and lower the open fingers to grasp height. Small lateral correction remains uncertain.
Make final millimeter-scale centering and close around the handle; retention will be checked during a lift.
Lift the closed grasp and begin carrying the mallet toward the leftmost key. Check visible retention before striking.
Mallet is visibly retained. Carry it above the first red key with the shaft pointing right, keeping the left wrist in its own workspace.
Replan after the continuity guard with smaller sideways increments. Align the mallet tip over the first red key without further forward reach.
Lower the retained mallet toward the first red key, with a small forward correction to keep its tip inside the key's near edge.
Tap the first red key vertically, then lift the mallet by 45 mm before progressing to the next key.
Move the already-lifted mallet one key to the right, then descend onto the orange key. Keep the closed left grasp and fixed wrist orientation.
Finish the orange-key tap, lift 48 mm, and move above the yellow key. Retained mallet remains visible between the fingers.
Refine tip alignment over yellow, strike vertically, then lift 36 mm before moving farther right.
Advance from yellow to green while lifted, tap green, and raise the mallet 40 mm. Keep the left wrist on the left side.
Complete the green-key lift using smaller increments after the guard, then move to the cyan key and tap it.
Retract from the reach limit while yawing the mallet forward to preserve tip placement. Approach cyan with smaller increments; do not strike during repositioning.
The prior attempt executed zero steps. Use 2–3 mm retraction increments and small yaw changes to restore a reach margin before advancing.
Center the mallet over cyan, tap downward, then lift 40 mm. The retracted arm now has a safer reach margin.
Move the lifted tip from cyan to the blue key, slightly retracting the wrist while turning the shaft forward, then tap blue.
Lift from blue by 40 mm, then pitch the mallet head slightly down relative to the fingers to avoid key contact by the gripper. Large tracking residual suggests contact.
Advance to the seventh, purple key with a retracted elbow-up approach, then lower the pitched mallet tip for the tap.
Complete the purple-key tap, lift 40 mm, and position the mallet over the final magenta key while keeping the left wrist left of center.
After the continuity interruption, retract first with smaller increments, then turn the shaft and advance toward the last key without crossing the wrist over center.
Tap the final magenta key with a slight forward correction, then lift the mallet 50 mm to clear it.
Retract the left wrist to restore joint margin after the interrupted final lift, keeping the mallet closed and clearing the keys.
Return above the leftmost key for a cleaner left-to-right pass; pitch the mallet tip slightly below the fingers to avoid the prior gripper-contact uncertainty.
Descend onto the first red key with the tip centered farther inside the key and the fingers held above it.
Lift 40 mm after the red-key contact, then move to orange while clear and begin its vertical descent.
Correct the tip's visible leftward offset before descending onto orange. Hold briefly at the tap to inspect contact and mallet retention.
Lift 40 mm from orange, shift to the center of yellow, and begin the next controlled tap.
Complete the yellow-key tap, lift 40 mm, and move the cleared mallet over green with a small wrist retraction.
Center the ball over green, complete a 40 mm down-and-up stroke, and retain the mallet for the next key.
Move to cyan with a small retraction and pitch adjustment for reach margin, then tap with the mallet tip below the fingers.
Lift clear of cyan by 40 mm and shift to blue, keeping the wrist retracted and the left grasp closed.
Strike the centered blue key and lift 40 mm before advancing to purple; keep both arm configurations continuous.
Advance the cleared mallet to purple with a slight retraction, tap vertically, and start lifting. Keep the left wrist left of center.
Finish the purple-key lift above 25 mm, retract for reach margin, and bring the ball over the final magenta key without crossing the wrist over center.
Replan with smaller diagonal increments after the guard. Retract and rotate gradually to position the lifted tip above the last key while preserving joint margin.
Strike the final magenta key with the tip centered inside its edge, then lift 42 mm while retracting slightly to maintain joint margin.
The second left-to-right pass and final lift have been executed. Retract the retained mallet away from the keys while keeping it elevated and restoring elbow margin.
Withdraw the raised mallet farther from the instrument into the left workspace, avoiding further incidental key contact.
